concepts.name: Composition and appointment of Supreme Court judges
concepts.description: Origin of the Supreme Court, its strength over time, the Judges cases, the NJAC verdict and the appointment of the Chief Justice of India.
concepts.idea: The Constitution requires consultation; the Court itself has turned consultation into the collegium and fixed seniority for the Chief Justice.
concepts.rule: The Supreme Court (inaugurated 28 January 1950) succeeded the Federal Court and replaced the Privy Council. Strength: 8 originally, now 34 (CJI plus 33). Judges are appointed by the President after consultation; CJI consultation is obligatory for other judges. First Judges case 1981: consultation is not concurrence; Second 1993: concurrence, CJI advice binding after consulting two seniormost colleagues; Third 1998: collegium of four seniormost judges. The 99th Amendment and NJAC Act 2014 were struck down in 2015 (Fourth Judges case). The seniormost judge alone is to be CJI (Second Judges case).
concepts.example: Before the Second Judges case the Government could appoint a junior judge as CJI, as in 1973 and 1977; since 1993 the seniormost judge alone is appointed.

questions.a: A single integrated system of courts, adopted from the Government of India Act of 1935, enforces both Central and state laws
o: A single integrated system of courts, adopted from the Government of India Act of 1935, enforces both Central and state laws

Each state has its own Supreme Court, which finally decides cases arising under the state laws
The high courts enforce the state laws while the Supreme Court enforces only the Central laws
questions.e: p.414: India has an integrated judicial system with the Supreme Court at the top; the single system enforces both Central and state laws, unlike the double system of the USA.
w: This describes the double system of the USA, which India does not follow (p.414).
There is one Supreme Court for the whole country; no separate state Supreme Courts exist (p.414).

questions.q:
With reference to the origin of the Supreme Court of India, consider the following statements:

1. The Supreme Court succeeded the Federal Court of India, which had been established under the Government of India Act of 1935.
2. The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is greater than that of the Federal Court because it has replaced the British Privy Council as the highest court of appeal.
3. The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 26 January 1950, the day the Constitution came into force.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.414 states this. Statement 2 is correct: p.414 gives exactly this reason. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.414 says it was inaugurated on 28 January 1950. So the correct option is '1 and 2 only'.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.414
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.414
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.414

questions.q:
With reference to the strength of the Supreme Court of India, consider the following statements:

1. The Constitution originally fixed the strength of the Court at seven judges, including the Chief Justice.
2. The Parliament increased the number of judges other than the Chief Justice to ten in 1956.
3. The Parliament raised the number of judges other than the Chief Justice to thirty-three in 2008.
4. Article 124(1) permits the Parliament to prescribe by law a number larger than seven other judges.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.414 says eight, that is one Chief Justice and seven other judges. Statement 2 is correct: p.414 and Table 26.2 (p.426) give ten in 1956. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.414: thirty in 2008; thirty-three came in 2019. Statement 4 is correct: p.427 (note to Table 26.2) quotes Article 124(1): 'until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number'. So the correct option is '2 and 4 only'.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.414
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.414
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.414

2. The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President after consultation with such judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts as the President deems necessary.

2. In the Second Judges case (1993), the Court held that the advice of the Chief Justice is not binding on the President.
3. In the Third Judges case (1998), the Court said that the sole opinion of the Chief Justice of India is enough to constitute the consultation process.
4. The Third Judges case arose from a reference made by the President under Article 143 on the consultation process.

Statement 3 is incorrect: p.414: the sole opinion does not constitute consultation; a collegium of four seniormost judges is needed. Statement 4 is correct: p.429, footnote 2: the President sought the Court's opinion under Article 143. So the correct option is '1 and 4 only'.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.414

concepts.name: Qualifications, oath, salaries, tenure and removal of judges
concepts.description: Who can be a Supreme Court judge, what the judge swears, pay and pension, retirement age and the removal procedure under the Constitution and the Judges Enquiry Act.
concepts.idea: A judge needs citizenship plus one of three routes, serves till 65 and can be removed only on proved misbehaviour or incapacity by a special-majority address of both Houses.
concepts.rule: Qualifications: citizen of India; five years as a High Court judge, or ten years as a High Court advocate, or a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President; no minimum age. Oath before the President or his appointee. Salaries and pension are fixed by Parliament and cannot be varied to the judge's disadvantage except during a financial emergency; pension is 50 per cent of last salary. Holds office till 65; resigns to the President. Removal by the President after an address of each House by special majority in the same session, on proved misbehaviour or incapacity; Judges Enquiry Act 1968: motion signed by 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members, three-member committee. No judge has been impeached; Justice V. Ramaswami's motion was defeated in the Lok Sabha.
concepts.example: In 1991-93 the committee found Justice Ramaswami guilty, yet the motion failed in the Lok Sabha and he was not removed.

three judges of the Supreme Court nominated by the Chief Justice of India from the seniormost

concepts.name: Acting, ad hoc and retired judges, seat, procedure and independence
concepts.description: Temporary arrangements for judges, the seat and procedure of the Court, and the nine safeguards of its independence.
concepts.idea: The Court can be staffed temporarily by acting, ad hoc and retired judges, and nine constitutional features protect it from the executive and the legislature.
concepts.rule: The President appoints an acting Chief Justice when the office is vacant or the CJI is absent or unable to act. The CJI can appoint a High Court judge as an ad hoc judge when quorum is lacking, after consulting that High Court's chief justice and with the President's consent, and can request a retired judge with the consent of the President and the person. Delhi is the seat; other places only optionally with the President's approval. Constitutional cases and Article 143 references need at least five judges. Independence: appointment in consultation with the judiciary, security of tenure, fixed service conditions, expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund, no discussion of conduct, ban on practice after retirement, contempt power, staff appointed by the CJI, jurisdiction cannot be curtailed.
concepts.example: A High Court judge sitting as an ad hoc judge must give priority to the Supreme Court sittings over his own High Court duties.

concepts.name: Original and writ jurisdiction
concepts.description: The Supreme Court as a federal court with exclusive original jurisdiction, its exclusions, its concurrent writ jurisdiction for fundamental rights, and how Parliament can enlarge its powers.
concepts.idea: Federal disputes go only to the Supreme Court in the first instance; fundamental-rights petitions can go to it or a high court.
concepts.rule: Original jurisdiction is exclusive in disputes between the Centre and states or among states, where a legal right (not a political question) is at stake; private citizens cannot sue under it. It excludes pre-Constitution treaties, inter-state river disputes, Finance Commission matters and certain adjustments of expenses and pensions. The first suit (1961) was West Bengal v. the Centre on the Coal Bearing Areas Act, dismissed. concepts.name: Appellate jurisdiction and special leave
concepts.description: The four heads of appeal to the Supreme Court: constitutional, civil, criminal and special leave, with their certificate rules and limits.
concepts.idea: Constitutional and civil appeals need a High Court certificate; some criminal appeals lie as of right; special leave is a discretionary power over any court or tribunal except military ones.
concepts.rule: The Supreme Court is primarily a court of appeal (it replaced the Privy Council). Constitutional appeals need a High Court certificate of a substantial question of law requiring interpretation of the Constitution; civil appeals need a certificate of a substantial question of general importance (the Rs 20,000 limit was removed by the 30th Amendment 1972). Criminal appeals lie as of right, without a certificate, where the High Court reversed an acquittal and imposed death, or tried the case itself and imposed death; in other cases the High Court may certify the case as fit for appeal; the 1970 enlargement added sentences of life or ten years; there is no right of appeal if the High Court acquitted. Special leave: discretionary, any judgement, any matter, any court or tribunal except military, used sparingly.
concepts.example: A death sentence imposed by a High Court after it reversed an acquittal can be taken to the Supreme Court as of right, without a certificate.

concepts.name: Advisory jurisdiction, court of record and contempt of court
concepts.description: Article 143 references and their non-binding opinions, the Court as a court of record, and the Contempt of Courts Act 1971.
concepts.idea: The President may consult the Court under Article 143 but is not bound by its opinion; the Court is a court of record that punishes contempt under the 1971 Act.
concepts.rule: Article 143 lets the President seek the Court's opinion on (a) a question of law or fact of public importance (the Court may refuse) and (b) a dispute from a pre-constitution treaty or sanad (the Court must reply). The opinion is advisory, not binding. The book lists fifteen references from the Delhi Laws Act (1951) to the 2G spectrum case (2012). As a court of record, its judgements are preserved as precedents and it punishes contempt (in 1991 extended to high courts, subordinate courts and tribunals). The Contempt of Courts Act 1971 followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee; civil and criminal contempt; punishment up to six months or Rs 2,000 or both; one-year limitation; fair reporting and criticism exempt; not for Nyaya Panchayats.
concepts.example: A President who disagrees with the Court's Article 143 opinion may still decline to follow it, since it is not a judicial pronouncement.

concepts.name: Judicial review, review jurisdiction, interpretation and other powers
concepts.description: Judicial review, review and curative petitions, doctrines of interpretation, other powers such as Article 141 binding law, and the comparison with the American Supreme Court.
concepts.idea: The Court can strike down unconstitutional laws, reconsider its own judgements, and its law binds all courts.
concepts.rule: Judicial review lets the Court declare ultra vires laws and executive orders of the Centre and states null and void. It can review its own judgements within thirty days before the same bench on new evidence, error on the face of the record or other sufficient reason; a curative petition on limited grounds (natural justice, miscarriage of justice, abuse of process, bias) survives a dismissed review. It is the ultimate interpreter of the Constitution, guided by doctrines such as severability and eclipse. Its other powers include enquiring into Public Service Commission members on a presidential reference (binding advice), withdrawing and transferring cases, binding all courts with its law and superintending all courts and tribunals. According to the book's Table 26.1, its judicial review is narrower than the American Court's and it follows 'procedure established by law' rather than 'due process of law'.
concepts.example: A law that violates the Constitution is declared void by the Court and the Government cannot enforce it.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.423 says so. Statement 2 is correct: p.423 says so. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.423: it covers both Central and state governments. So the correct option is '1 and 2 only'.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.423
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.423
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.423

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a review petition before the Supreme Court:

1. It has to be filed within ninety days from the date of the judgement.
2. It should be submitted to the same judge or bench that delivered the judgement or order.
3. Discovery of new and important matter or evidence is a ground on which it is allowed.
4. The Court must always direct notice to the opposite party and cannot dismiss it at the first stage.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.424: it has to be filed within thirty days. Statement 2 is correct: p.424 says so. Statement 3 is correct: p.424 says so. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.424: the Court may either dismiss it or direct notice to the opposite party. So the correct option is '2 and 3 only'.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.424
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.424
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.424

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the curative petition:

1. It can be used to reconsider a final judgement even after a review petition has been dismissed.
2. Violation of the principles of natural justice is one of its grounds.
3. Discovery of new and important evidence is one of its grounds.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.424 says so. Statement 2 is correct: p.424 says so. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.424: that is a ground for review, not for a curative petition. So the correct option is '1 and 2 only'.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.424
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.424
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.424

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Supreme Court is the ultimate interpreter of the Constitution and is guided by a number of doctrines such as severability, eclipse and pith and substance.
2. The Supreme Court interprets the Constitution only by its literal words and applies no doctrine.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.424 says so. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.424: it applies various doctrines in interpreting the Constitution. So the answer is '1 only'.
w: '2 only': statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect: p.424
'Both 1 and 2': statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect: p.424
'Neither 1 nor 2': statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect: p.424

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Supreme Court over other courts:

1. Its law is binding on all courts in India.
2. All authorities, civil and judicial, in the country should act in aid of the Supreme Court.
3. It has the power of judicial superintendence and control over all the courts and tribunals functioning in the entire territory of the country.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 2 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 3 is correct: p.425 says so. So the correct option is '1, 2 and 3'.
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.425
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.425
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.425

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the members of the Public Service Commissions:

1. The Supreme Court enquires into the conduct of the chairman and members of the UPSC, SPSC or JSPSC on a reference made by the President.
2. If it finds them guilty, it removes them from office on its own order.
3. The advice of the Supreme Court in this matter is not binding on the President.
4. The enquiry can cover a member of a Joint State Public Service Commission also.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.425: it can only recommend their removal to the President. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.425: the advice is binding on the President. Statement 4 is correct: p.425 names the JSPSC. So the correct option is '1 and 4 only'.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.425
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.425
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.425

questions.q:
According to Table 26.1 of the chapter, consider the following statements comparing the Indian and American Supreme Courts:

1. The scope of judicial review of the Indian Supreme Court is limited, while that of the American Supreme Court is very wide.
2. The Indian Supreme Court defends rights according to the 'due process of law', while the American one follows the 'procedure established by law'.
3. The Indian Supreme Court has judicial superintendence over the state high courts because of the integrated judicial system, which the American Supreme Court lacks over state courts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.426 (Table 26.1). Statement 2 is incorrect: p.426 (Table 26.1): it is the other way round. Statement 3 is correct: p.426 (Table 26.1). So the correct option is '1 and 3 only'.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.426
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.426
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.426

questions.q:
According to Table 26.3 (Articles related to the Supreme Court at a glance), consider the following statements:

1. Article 137 deals with special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court.
2. Article 139A deals with the transfer of certain cases.
3. Article 141 deals with the enforcement of decrees and orders of the Supreme Court.
4. Article 144 deals with civil and judicial authorities acting in aid of the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.428: Article 137 deals with the review of judgments or orders; special leave is Article 136. Statement 2 is correct: p.428 lists so. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.429: Article 141 is the law declared by the Supreme Court being binding; enforcement of decrees is Article 142. Statement 4 is correct: p.429 lists so. So the correct option is '2 and 4 only'.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.428
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.428
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.428

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the other powers of the Supreme Court:

1. It can withdraw the cases pending before the high courts only with the consent of the concerned high court.
2. It can transfer a case or appeal pending before one high court to another high court.
3. Its decree or order is enforceable throughout the country.
4. Its decrees are enforceable throughout the country only with the concurrence of the state governments.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.425: it is authorised to withdraw such cases and dispose them by itself; no consent is mentioned. Statement 2 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 3 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.425: its decree or order is enforceable throughout the country and all authorities must act in its aid. So the correct option is '2 and 3 only'.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.425
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.425
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.425

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Judicial review is the power to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders.
2. A review petition has to be filed within thirty days of the judgement.
3. A curative petition can be filed before the review petition is decided.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.423 says so. Statement 2 is correct: p.424 says so. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.424: it can be used even after the dismissal of the review petition. So only two of the statements are correct.
w: Miscount: 2 of the statements are correct, so 'None' is wrong: p.423/424
Miscount: 2 of the statements are correct, so 'Only one' is wrong: p.423/424
Miscount: 2 of the statements are correct, so 'All three' is wrong: p.423/424

questions.q:
According to Table 26.1 of the chapter, consider the following statements comparing the Indian and American Supreme Courts:

1. The jurisdiction and powers of the Indian Supreme Court can be enlarged by the Parliament.
2. The jurisdiction and powers of the American Supreme Court can be enlarged by the Congress.
3. The Indian Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction, while the American one has none.
4. The American Supreme Court has the power of superintendence over state high courts.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.426 (Table 26.1). Statement 2 is incorrect: p.426 (Table 26.1): they are limited to those conferred by the Constitution. Statement 3 is correct: p.426 (Table 26.1). Statement 4 is incorrect: p.426 (Table 26.1): it has no such power because of the double judicial system. So only two of the statements are correct.
w: Miscount: 2 of the statements are correct, so 'Only one' is wrong: p.426
Miscount: 2 of the statements are correct, so 'Only three' is wrong: p.426
Miscount: 2 of the statements are correct, so 'All four' is wrong: p.426

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The advice of the Supreme Court on the misbehaviour of a Public Service Commission member is binding on the President.
2. The Supreme Court can withdraw cases pending before the high courts and dispose them by itself.
3. The decree or order of the Supreme Court is enforceable throughout the country.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 2 is correct: p.425 says so. Statement 3 is correct: p.425 says so. So all three of the statements are correct.
w: Miscount: 3 of the statements are correct, so 'Only two' is wrong: p.425
Miscount: 3 of the statements are correct, so 'Only one' is wrong: p.425
Miscount: 3 of the statements are correct, so 'None' is wrong: p.425

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts in India.
Statement-II: All authorities, civil and judicial, in the country should act in aid of the Supreme Court.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.425. Statement-II is correct: p.425. The duty of authorities to act in aid concerns enforcement of the Court's orders; it is a separate power and does not explain why its law binds all courts. Article 144 (p.429, Table 26.3) deals with civil and judicial authorities acting in aid of the Supreme Court.
w: Acting in aid is about enforcement, a separate provision (Article 144), not the reason for binding force (p.425, 429).
II is correct: p.425 states the duty to act in aid.
I is correct: p.425 says its law is binding on all courts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: According to Table 26.1, the scope of judicial review of the Indian Supreme Court is wider than that of the American Supreme Court.
Statement-II: According to Table 26.1, the Indian Supreme Court defends the rights of the citizen according to the procedure established by law.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: p.426 says the Indian scope is limited and the American one very wide. Statement-II is correct: p.426.
w: I is false, so II cannot explain it (p.426).
I is false, not merely unconnected (p.426).
II is the correct statement and I is the incorrect one (p.426).

questions.q:
Match the term in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I
A. Review petition
B. Curative petition
C. Judicial review
D. Article 141

List-II
1. Examination of the constitutionality of enactments and executive orders
2. Law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts
3. Limited grounds such as bias of the judge, after a review petition is dismissed
4. Filed within thirty days before the same judge or bench
questions.e: p.423-424 and p.429: judicial review examines constitutionality; a review petition is filed within thirty days before the same bench; a curative petition is on limited grounds; Article 141 makes the Court's law binding.
w: Interchanges A and B: review is within thirty days; the curative petition has limited grounds (p.424).
Interchanges C and D: judicial review examines constitutionality; Article 141 makes law binding (p.423, 429).
Interchanges B and C: the curative petition has limited grounds and judicial review examines constitutionality (p.423-424).
